headline: Themed Floors: The Arcade offers a first look at AI agents off the clock
summary: A developer is building a virtual world where players and AI agents coexist, now previewing 'Themed Floors' that transform spaces like an office into an arcade with a single tap.
details: A developer is creating a virtual world where human players and AI-agent avatars share the same interactive space. This initiative aims to build dynamic environments where AI agents can operate independently.

A first look at "THEMED FLOORS: THE ARCADE" showcases how an office floor can instantly transform into an arcade. This feature is part of a larger system that will include nine distinct floor themes, such as Lounge and Night Club.

The preview footage was captured in-engine from a private filming build, with player inputs scripted for demonstration purposes. Connected AI agents were directed to the arcade, where their avatars autonomously selected machines through the world's simulation.

While "Themed Floors" and "The Arcade" are not yet available on the public play site, the trailer concludes with a "Coming soon" message. Users can currently join the existing virtual world at play.myvirtualworld.ai to experience the shared space.

headline_marked: [[Smart contract escrow and AI judges]] tested for crypto freelance work, improving transparency
headline: Smart contract escrow and AI judges tested for crypto freelance work, improving transparency
summary: A new system leverages smart contracts and decentralized AI judges on the Base network to ensure fair evaluations and automatic payouts for crypto freelance bounties, eliminating subjective reviews and payment delays.
details: Freelancers in the Web3 ecosystem often face issues with opaque review processes and delayed payments for their work. This can lead to frustration, with projects sometimes being held up for weeks or rejected on subjective grounds, preventing bounty payouts.

A new workflow, exemplified by Verdikta Bounties on the Base network, aims to solve this trust problem. Before a bounty opens, employers lock payment funds into a smart contract escrow and define clear evaluation criteria and passing scores upfront.

Once work is submitted, a panel of decentralized AI judges independently assesses it against these criteria, providing public, written scores and reasons. If the average score meets the threshold, the smart contract automatically releases funds to the first successful submitter.

This mechanism offers significant advantages for verifiable digital tasks, eliminating debates with project teams and waiting for manual payouts. Workers also benefit from zero platform fees, only needing to cover Base network gas and a small oracle evaluation fee (around 0.00024 ETH).

However, the system has limitations: AI judges are unsuitable for physical work requiring on-site verification, and evaluation quality heavily depends on how clearly the bounty creator defines the initial criteria. Overly abstract task descriptions can lead to suboptimal scoring.
